Read and write PDM for PCs input files

Source: R/pdm_inp.R
read_pdm_inp.Rd

read_pdm_inp() reads the model of a PDM for PCs *.inp file into a configuration, so a model calibrated in PDM for PCs can be run, scored and compared with one calibrated here (see compare_calibrations()). write_pdm_inp() writes a configuration as a *.inp file that PDM for PCs can load (Model > Load Previous PDM Configuration).

Usage

read_pdm_inp(path, dt = 0.25)

write_pdm_inp(
  config,
  path,
  title,
  event,
  stations = c(flow = "FLOW", rain = "RAIN", pet = "SIN CURVE", daily_rain = "NULL"),
  optimised = character(0)
)

Arguments

path

Path of the *.inp file.

dt

Model time step, hours.

config

A configuration list, or a FlodePdmModel.

title

First line of the file: the model or catchment name.

event

Start and end of the calibration event (period), as two times (POSIXct, or text such as "2010-10-01 09:00", in UTC). PDM for PCs needs at least one.

stations

Named character vector of the series names PDM for PCs will ask for: flow, rain, pet and daily_rain.

optimised

Names, as in the file (rainfac, cmax, kb and so on), of the parameters to mark for optimisation; none by default.

Value

read_pdm_inp(): a configuration list for pdm_from_config(), with attributes title, stations, events (a data frame of start and end), optimised (the file's names of the parameters marked for optimisation), theta (the initial soil fraction of a split model, if given) and notes. write_pdm_inp(): the path, invisibly.

Details

What is read. The parameter list (by name, so its order does not matter), the model structure line (loss runoff surface base tdly), the catchment area, the groundwater extension block ('GW') with its well datum, and, as attributes, the title, the stations, the event periods and which parameters were marked for optimisation (indx = 1). Error prediction, forecast and rating settings are not part of the simulation model; they are noted in attribute notes and otherwise ignored, as are raingauge weights: give the catchment rainfall in the forcing.

Conventions of PDM for PCs. These follow the manual and are applied in both directions:

  • the cubic store's kb in the file is the cube root of the time constant used (kb = 13 in the file is 2197 h mm^2 here);

  • k2 = 0 means two equal surface reservoirs, k2 = k1;

  • tdly in the structure line is either the delay in hours or, when negative, the position of the tdly parameter in the list;

  • rainfac is the rainfall factor fc, qconst the constant flow qc (m3/s);

  • lognormal (loss 5) reads cmin and b as the mean and standard deviation of log capacity, and exponential (loss 6) reads cmin as the mean capacity;

  • the cubic store is stepped by Smith's method, as in PDM for PCs.

The time step is not in the file. PDM for PCs takes it from the model set-up, so give it as dt (15 minutes by default).

Not supported, and refused with a message rather than guessed: several hydrological zones; demand recharge and the unrestricted split (runoff models 2 to 4); the power distribution (loss 4); exponential stores; a cubic surface store; and constant or pass-through stores (types 0 and -1).

To do: the exponential store. It is a PDM option (Moore, 2007), and pdmS7 runs, calibrates and forecasts with it, and the structure recommendation may choose it. Its code and parameter layout in a PDM for PCs input file are still to be confirmed, so write_pdm_inp() refuses it for now. It will be added once an example file with an exponential store has been checked.

References

UKCEH (2022). PDM for PCs, version 3.0.3: Configuration Guide, section 2.3 and Appendix A.1.

Examples

cfg <- pdm_presets("standard")
cfg$area_km2 <- 36.7
cfg$dt <- 0.25
path <- tempfile(fileext = ".inp")
write_pdm_inp(cfg, path, title = "Example Brook: standard PDM",
              event = c("2010-10-01 09:00", "2020-10-01 09:00"))
back <- read_pdm_inp(path, dt = 0.25)
back$groundwater
#> $type
#> [1] "cubic"
#> 
#> $kb
#> [1] 10000
#> 
#> $solver
#> [1] "smith"
#>
